rationale: The student confuses the face number with the elapsed minute value, missing the underlying structure of skip-counting by 5s. Practicing jumps of 5 along a number line clearly models how each successive clock number represents an additional 5 minutes.
intent: Practice skip-counting forward by 5s starting from 0 up to 60. Use multiples such as 5, 10, 15, 25, 30, and 35, avoiding the target problem of 4 jumps (20 minutes) so as not to give away the immediate answer to 3:04 vs 3:20.

data.title: Clock Face Hops by 5s!
data.description: Learn to tell time to the nearest 5 minutes by hopping around the clock face with a kangaroo!

character.imagePrompt: A friendly cartoon kangaroo wearing a clock tie, ready to hop across clock numbers.

challenges.instruction: The kangaroo is at 5 minutes. Where is the next landing?
challenges.hint: Count up by 5 more! 5 plus 5 equals...

challenges.instruction: The kangaroo is at 10 minutes. Where is the next landing?
The kangaroo is at 15 minutes. Where is the next landing?
challenges.hint: What comes after 15 when counting by 5s?

challenges.instruction: The kangaroo is at 25 minutes. Where is the next landing?
The kangaroo is at 30 minutes. Where is the next landing?
The kangaroo is at 35 minutes. Where is the next landing?

judgement.reasoning: The student confuses the face number with minutes (reading the minute hand pointing to 4 as 4 minutes instead of 20). Skip-counting by 5 on an open number line without linking jump numbers (1, 2, 3, 4...) or clock face numbers directly to the minutes counted does not bridge the core misconception (that clock numeral 4 represents 20 minutes). It is merely rote skip-counting by 5s. Furthermore, c3 specifically prompts the jump from 15 to 20, leaking the exact answer needed for the student's problem.
judgement.verdict: This detour only practices rote skip counting without connecting clock numerals to 5-minute increments, and it directly computes the 20-minute mark from the original error.
